mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the permission matrix fact lets Alloy assign any combination to PermMatrix.Allowed, including giving customers PostDecision or stripping BankStaff of OpPostDecision — violating least-privilege assertions.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermissionMatrixViolation { CustomerRole -> OpPostDecision in PermMatrix.Allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows two AuditEntry atoms to share the same (auditApp, eventType) pair, modelling an overwrite of an existing audit record — exactly what AppendOnly and FR_016 are supposed to prevent.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj ae1, ae2: AuditEntry | ae1.auditApp = ae2.auditApp and ae1.eventType = ae2.eventType }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the partial-unique-index constraint, allowing the same customer to own two PendingReview applications simultaneously — the exact violation FR-005 and SC-001 are designed to catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OnePendingViolation { some disj la1, la2: LoanApplication | la1.appOwner = la2.appOwner and la1.appStatus = PendingReview and la2.appStatus = PendingReview }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact dissolves the PK constraint on decisions.application_id, allowing two Decision atoms to reference the same LoanApplication — the concurrent-decision scenario SC-005 explicitly prohibits.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DuplicateDecisionViolation { some disj d1, d2: Decision | d1.decidedApp = d2.decidedApp }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact lets Alloy set any AccessAttempt.response freely, including giving a customer Resp200 for an application they do not own — violating FR-013 and the no-information-leakage contract.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnershipLeakViolation { some a: AccessAttempt | a.caller.userRole = CustomerRole and a.caller != a.target.appOwner and a.response = Resp200 }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows a BankStaff actor to be recorded on a Submitted audit entry, or a Customer actor on an Approved/Rejected entry — misattribution that FR-016 and AttributionCorrectness are designed to prevent.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionViolation { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.eventType = EvtSubmitted and ae.actor.userRole = BankStaffRole }
